title: The Pendulum in International Affairs
summary:
This process boosted economic growth in the emerging nations where the work was done,
increased savings and competitiveness for manufacturers and importers, and
provided low-priced goods to consumers. As each country benefited from the growth of manufacturing, the supply of labor got tighter,
and workers became able to demand higher wages. Wages may have risen locally, but as a consequence, the search for low-margin, low-skill
work moved on to new low-cost venues.

reader_summary.headline: This is the memo by Howard Marks, The Pendulum in International Affairs.
reader_summary.overview: This is the memo by Howard Marks, The Pendulum in International Affairs. As regular readers of my memos and books know, I'm strongly interested in, you might say obsessed with, the concept of the pendulum. The following is only a partial list of my writings on the subject.

key_points.text: My second memo, written in April 1991, was creatively titled First Quarter Performance.
key_points.evidence_quote: My second memo, written in April 1991, was creatively titled First Quarter Performance.

key_points.text: It talked about the oscillation in securities markets between euphoria and depression, between celebrating positive developments and obsessing over negatives.
key_points.evidence_quote: It talked about the oscillation in securities markets between euphoria and depression, between celebrating positive developments and obsessing over negatives, and thus between overpriced and underpriced assets.

key_points.text: On regulation, written in March 2011, discussed the outlook for rulemaking stemming from the global financial crisis.
key_points.evidence_quote: On regulation, written in March 2011, discussed the outlook for rulemaking stemming from the global financial crisis.

key_points.text: I said future developments were likely to be driven by the long-term pendulum-like swing in attitudes on that subject.
key_points.evidence_quote: I said future developments were likely to be driven by the long-term pendulum-like swing in attitudes on that subject.
